newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND HOPES FOR EMU DEAL IN 96 ON STABILITY PACT.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND HOPES FOR EMU DEAL IN 96 ON STABILITY PACT.

text.p: Finland hopes that the European Union will reach full agreement this year on a budget stability pact for countries joining monetary union, a Finnish finance ministry official said on Friday.
"We are still hopeful that a political agreement will be reached on the stability pact this year," finance ministry official Lasse Aarnio told a news conference.
"But according to the original plan the pact will not be legally ratified until next year," he added.
A stability pact is to be put in place to enforce sustained budgetary rigour among governments taking part in the planned third stage of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
Aarnio said there was still disagreement on the circumstances under which a country could avoid sanctions if it failed to live to the rules of the stability pact.
"We think there should be strict rules which could be implemented depending on each country's situation," Aarnio said.
"We oppose strict numerical sanctions because the member countries' economic conditions differ dramatically," he said.
An excessive public deficit could lead to implementation of sanctions.

The EU Commission has proposed that the sanctions would be made up of a fixed element equivalent to 0.2 percent of GDP of the offending country plus the equivalent of one tenth of the difference between the actual deficit and the three percent reference value.
In order to avoid counter-productive effects of sanctions, an overall ceiling of 0.5 percent of GDP would be set.
German insistence on a tough budget stability pact has led EU officials to scale back their predictions for a full agreement this year.
Some believe that EU leaders will only agree a broad political statement in favour of a pact when they meet at a summit in Dublin on December 13 and 14.
The preparations of the stability pact will be discussed at the European Union finance ministers ECOFIN meeting on Novemeber 11.
